day, also before a meal, (a. 15 d.) ni\co,'& Nsil.sea
rn Jal, so violent that the pit feels sore and aching. Nausea
Niusen with expectoration of much mucus, without
SuX' Qualmishness in the stomach, in the forenoon.


63

Nausea in the stomach, with vertigo and oppression of
the pit of the stomach, and eructations lasting of phos-
phorus. Constant nausea, (a. 1 1 d.) Nausea almost
the whole day. Nausea with great thirst. Nausea, noon
and afternoon, going off after drinking. Nausea, in the
evening when in bed, making her speech faint. Nausea
the whole day, and vomiting in the evening. Nausea,
late in the evening, unto fainting and vomiting. Nausea
and inclination to vomit, unto fainting, either in the fore-
noon or evening. Nausea and inclination to vomit, in the
morning, until breakfast. Nausea unto vomiting, and fre-
quent inclinations to faint, with dull pressure in the pit of
the stomach, making every external covering intolerable,
(a. 41 h.) Water-brash. Water-brash after a meal,
with eructalions, nausea and flow of water from the mouth.
Vomiting, several times. Suffering the most horrible
tortures, he tried in vain to vomit, nothing relieved him
except drinking cold water. Empty vomiting. Violent
vomiting. Vomiting, accompanied with excessive weak-
ness, small, quick pulse, and pains in the abdomen ; death.
Continual vomiting ; internal spasms, absence of mind,
paralysis of the arm, death. Vomiting and nausea when
riding in a carriage. Vomiting of the ingesta, in the
evening. Vomiting of mucus, with taste of olive-oil, in
the night. Vomiting of bile several limes. Vomiting of
bile, for 18 hours ; 24 hours after nausea unto vomiting,
and loss of appetite, with natural taste in the mouth, (a.
18 d.) Vomiting of bile, the whole night. Sour, bilious
vomiting, towards evening, preceded by vertigo with
nausea ; at the same time the hands and then the feet
became icy cold and completely numb ; cold sweat on the
forehead ; after several attacks of vomiting during the
space of two hours, he had two natural stools ; nausea
and coldness disappeared only after lying down, (26. d.)
Pains in the stomach, with nausea and desire to vomit.
Qua mishness in the pit of the stomach, and soon after
shuddering.

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
The region of the stomach is painful to the
touch. The stomach feels empty and fasting. Painful-
ness of the stomach when walking. Spoiled, weak stom-
ach, for a long time. Weak digestion. He digests with

64 PHOSPHORUS.

difficulty those things which he used to eat without any
trouble. Pain in the stomach, as if replete, until evening.
Violent pain in the stomach, gradually extending over the
whole abdomen, with vomiting, first of greenish, then black-
ish substances. Pressure at a small place of the stomach,
and at the same time in the right temple. Pressure in the

sections.label: stomach
sections.text:
Pressure over the stomach. Pressure in the
region of the cardiac orifice, especially when swallowing
bread, which appears to remain lodged there. Continual
pressure in the pit of the stomach, even before breaklast,
but most when sitting. Pressure over the pit of the stom-
ach, as of a large body, with coldness, (immediately.)
Pressure in the stomach, in the morning when in bed, Ja.
8 d ) Pressure in the stomach, in the evening, (a. 2 d.)
Pressure in the stomach after a meal, as if it contained a
load. Excessive pressure in and over the pit of the stom-
ach, afterwards in the whole sternum and in the region ot
the ribs, arresting the breathing, equally so when walking
or sitting, (a. 2 h) Repletion in the stomach Pufhness
of the stomach and abdomen. Cramp-feeling in the
stomach, pit of the stomach and chest, resembling a chilly
tremulousness. Cramps in the stomach. Pain in the
siomach, as if pressed together, in the morning when in
bed, after sweating. Tensive contraction of the stomach,
with sourish eructations. Contractive pinching in the
siomach, (a. 6 d.) Contraction and gnawing in the stom-
ach. Griping in the region of the stomach, in paroxysms,
Sting some Minutes, (22 d.) Drawing and stitching
in the stomach, when riding in a carriage. Rawing
pain in the pit of the stomach, extending into the chest
Cuttincr in the region of the stomach. Stitches o er
the stomach and 'through the abdomen, which then be-
came enlarged. Stitching in the pit of the stomach, ar-
resTm ' the Lathing, going off by eructations every even-
ine Stitch in the region of the stomach. Rumbling in
he stomach, or sensation as if bubbles burst in the stom-
ach Feelin- of coldness in the stomach, sometimes alter-
ing with heat. Violent, burning heat in the stomach,
sometimes issuing from the mouth like gas. Burning m
T s Zach, (a lOd.) Violent burning in the stomach
ltd bowels.' Violent burning in the ^stomach .^«JJ
thirst, anguish and convulsions of the face, violent thirst,


G5

cold limbs, clear, running eyes, pale lips, weak pulse, van-
ishing of strength, death. "Burning and cutting in the re-
gion of the stomach. Burning in ihe stomach and intesti-
nal canal. Inflammation of the stomach. Inflammation
and gangrene of the stomach and intestinal canal, with
violent burning and cutting. Burning, and oppressive
weight in the stomach.

sections.label: Abdomen
sections.text:
Violent pain in the left hypochondria, he
was not able to stoop, to lie on the right side. Anxiousness
under the left side of the chest, with bilter eructations
every day. Stitches under the left chest, with much anxi-
ety. Sensitiveness of the region of the liver ; when touch-
ing it, one experiences a dull pressure in it, especially when
lying upon the right side.' Stitches in the region of the
liver. Drawing cutting below the short ribs, during a walk.
Incarceration of flatulence under the ribs, with oppression
of the chest. Drawing aching pain in the epigastrium,
and as if the place were sore. Tension in the epigastri-
um, excited by every movement of the trunk. Violent
pinching in the left hypochondrium, towards the epigastri-
um ; afterwards sensation in that place as of something
living moving about there, when silting or standing. Pinch-
ing and cutting in the epigastrium, when walking. Colic,
in the morning. Colic in cool weather. Violent pain in
the. ivhole abdomen. Pressure in the abdomen, upon the
small of the back, as if caused by flatulence, with scanty
emission thereof. Pressure in the hypogastrium., in the
forenoon, and also after supper, (the first days.) Pressure
in the lower part of the abdomen, as if he would evacuate
the bowels. Spasmodic pressure, deep in the abdomen,
near the genital organs, in the morning when in bed.
Pressure in the abdomen, every morning when waking, as
if upon the bladder. Occasionally a very painful, con-
tractive pressure in the whole abdomen, of short duration.
Contractive sensation in the left side of the abdomen. Oc-
casional contractive pain in the intestines. Burning con-
tractive pain in the abdomen, as if the menses would make
their appearance at night ; (the menses had stopped a few
days previous ;) excessively painful, (a. 4 d.) Distension
of the abdomen, and sensation as of being distended, some-
times with pressure, sometimes relieved by motion, some-

66


times with difficulty of drawing a deep breath, or with
pain as if bruised in the small of the back and abdo-
men, when touching the parts. Bloated, extremely sen-
sitive abdomen. Oppressive fulness of the abdomen,
towards the stomach, especially oppressive after mid-
night. Sensation as if flamlence were rising from the
abdomen into the throat; this rising ceased as soon as
eructations set in. Incarceration of flatulence, with cold-
ness of the body and heat in the face. Distension of the
abdomen from flatulence, notwithstanding the emission of
much flatulence. Full, distended abdomen. Colic, ex-
tending from the region of the inguinal hernia to the stom-
ach. Flatulent colic, especially in the sides of the abdo-
men, as if the flatulence were incarcerated here and there ;
it passes off with great exertion in the space of twelve
hours in the shape of short, broken flatus. Oppressive in-
carceration of flatulence in the abdomen, when sitting or
lying, almost imperceptible when walking; sensation as if
the °abdomen were being drawn inwards, causing an un-
pleasant feeling. Spasmodic griping and contraction, ap-
parently in the uterus, in the evening, when stooping and
afterwards. Pinching in the abdomen, with discharge of
a brown fluid, followed by some burning and cessation of
the colic. Colic, followed by sour-smelling diarrhoeic stool,
jeavino- some tenesmus and burning. Violent cutting in
the abdomen, followed by discharge of liquid stool, jewing
out suddenly. Fine stinging in the left side of the abdo-
'men. Stitching colic, with pale complexion, chilliness
and headache, at noon, (a. 12 d.) Occasional transverse
stitches in the abdomen. Jerking and stitching in the hy-
pocrastriiim, in the morning. Occasionally a pinching
ierk in the hypogastrium, followed by emission ot flatu-
lence. Pain, as if something in the abdomen had burst.
Pain above the right hip, in the abdomen, as if something
were swollen and injured; pain as if bruised when touch-
incr the part. Sore or inflammatory pain in the abdomen,
extending to the genital organs, especially painful when
touching the parts, as if the bowels were sore, with weak-
ness Sore and stitching pain in the abuomen, relieved by
Winer upon the abdomen. Cramp-colic, first in the right
side? afterwards towards the back, (also in the right tes u-
cle, and upwards towards the region of the stomach, with


67

sweat, loud moaning and distortion of the muscles of the
face, (a. 7 d.) Colic, as if diarrhoea would come on, short

i but recurring frequently ; afterwards great soreness above
the ilium, when pressing from without. Feeling of coldness,
and coldness in the abdomen. Heat in the abdomen and
face, in the morning. Burning and pressure in the abdo-
men. Feeling of emptiness in the abdomen, after emis-

I sion of much flatulence, (a. 9 d.) Great feeling of weak-

: ness in the abdomen and back, she had to lie down, (a. '28
d.) Relaxed feeling in the abdomen. Itching of the um-
bilicus, which cannot be removed by scratching, (a. 6 h.)

. Large yellow spot upon the abdomen, on the side of the
umbilicus. Two boils on the abdomen. Aching in the
left groin. Great pain in the region of the inguinal hernia,
even without touching, during the menses. Swelling of
the inguinal glands. Tumor in the groin, with burning
pain. Painful pressure towards both inguinal rings, during
an attack of flatulent colic, as if inguinal hernia would
form. Protrusion of the inguinal hernia, during soft stool ;
it is painful as if incarcerated, when stooping, touching it,
or when walking, or even when lying upon that side of the
abdomen ; it cannot be reduced with the hand. Rumbling
in the region of the inguinal hernia. Painful rumbling in
the abdomen. Emission of a quantity of flatulence.

sections.label: Stool
sections.text:
Emission of flatulence, shortly after, stool in

i small pieces, with prickling in the rectum, leaving the
parts sensitive n long while after. Desire for stool; how-
ever, only flatulence is emitted. No stool, or else delaying.
Constipation. No stool, daring the first days. Constipa-
tion for 6 days ; with pressure in the pit of the stomach
after a meal, distension of the abdomen, and incarceration
of flatulence, (a. 24 h.) Difficult expidsion of fences.
Stool with violent pressing, only a little piece being passed
at the time. Violent pressing, the stool not being hard.
Scanty stool, followed by discharge of blood from the anus.
Costiveness the first four days. Hard stool in small
lumps. Hard stool covered with mucus. Hard stool,
with cutting in ihe anus. Four good stools a day, only a
little each time. Pinching in the abdomen, after which
stool with contraction of the rectum ; in two hours another
evacuation, without pinching, preceded by copious emission

68


of flatulence, and followed by contraction of the anus, (1.
d.) Soft stool, with pressing and cutting, in the larger
intestines, (a. 2 d.) Flatulent distension of the abdomen ;
on the second day, when the flatus move about in the
abdomen, the intestines feel as if bruised ; on the third day
incarceration of flatulence in the right side, causing painful
pressure ; on the fourth day, incarceration of flatulence in
the right side of the abdomen, causing a pinching pain.
The stool feels hot when passing. Papescent stool at an
unusual period (the first days.) Diarrhoea with tenes-
mus of the rectum, for 16 days, relieved by coffee.
Half-liquid stool. Diarrhoea, with expulsion of ascandes.
Green stool (of a baby whose nurse had taken phosphorus.)
Green, rather loose stools. Green and black stools.
Gray stool. The loose stool is mixed with lumps of white
mucus. Shining stools. Heat in the body previous to

sections.label: stool
sections.text:
Stool is preceded by violent chilliness. Colic
previous to the hard stool. Stool is preceded by violent
contractive pain, with stitches in the rectum Sore pres-
sure at the anus, before and during the hard stool, ling-
ling and itching in the rectum during the soft stool.
Erosive vain in the rectum during the rather loose stool.
Darting pain, during stool, from the os coccygis through
the spine, as far as the vertex, the head being drawn back-,
wards by it. Protrusion of varices during stool, with
burnincr pain when touching them, or when sitting and
walking, (a. some hours.) Blood with the stool for two
mornings. Hemorrhage from the rectum, (a. some n.)
Hemorrhage from the rectum, during emission of
flatulence, (a 1 1 d.) Soreness of the rectum after stool.
Sharp scratching and burning at the anus, frequent y, alter
stool, with burning desire to urinate, without much urine
beincr passed. Tenesmus after stool. Frightful tenesmus
of the rectum, some time afier stool. Pain over the anus
after making a slight effort at stool, six days in succession,
(a 8 d ) Violent burning at the anus and rectum,
after a soft stool, and great weakness. Great relaxation
in the abdomen, after loose stool, (a. 3 d.) Giddy and
near fainting afier the second stool. Sour vomiting, or
retching after stool, some mornings in succession, (a- 14 d.)
Shortly after stool, a white, corrosive mucus is discharged


69

from the anus, (a. some h.) Tearing in the rectum.
Prickling at the anus, when walking. Violent pain at the
anus, as if the abdomen were being torn asunder, with
i cutting and movement, of flatulence in the abdomen, and
constant unsuccessful desire for stool ; heat in the hands,
and anxiety ; the pain was relieved by applying warm
clothes, (3. d.) Cutting in the anus and rectum, especially
in the evening, (a. 6, 7 d.) Prickings in the rectum, be-
tween the evacuations. Stitching in the anus. Burning
at the rectum. Tearings in the rectum and the geaital or-
gans, so violent that one comes near falling down. Con-
tinued cramp like pushing around the rectum. Severe,
troublesome cramp in the rectum, in the morning when in
bed. Sensation in the rectum in the evening, as if the
• passage of the faeces were prevented by something ob-
structing the rectum ; the stool not being hard. The
i rectum feels contracted ; during the passage of the faeces,
i which are not hard, an acrid sore pain is felt in the rectum,
i continuing for several hours and extending into the abdo-
: men. Sore pain ot the varices, for many days, when sit-
ting or lying down, with violent pressure and stitches in
the varices when rising. Gnawing and itching of the
anus, (a. 7 d.)

Urinary Organs. — Great desire for evacuating, the
bladder and the rectum, (a. 3 d:) Difficult emission of
I the urine, as if the passage were impeded. The urine
stops every moment, and refuses to come off; accom-
panied with puffiness. The emission of urine is impeded
by a dull pain in the hypogastrium, in the morning, when
in bed, preventing the emission of urine to the last drop ;
after short intervals he felt again a desire to emit urine ;
in this case it came off drop by drop and in small quantity,
(9. d.) Frequent emission of the ordinary quantity of
urine, five emissions in two hours, in the morning after
rising, for some days. Frequent micturition, little at a
time, (a. 40 h.) Profuse micturition. Increased emission
of dark-brown urine, smelling of gxrlick and sulphur.
Sudden desire to urinate, in the morning, (a. 3 weeks.)
He was unable to retain his urine, owing to a violent desire
to urinate. Frequent micturition in the night. Involun-
tary emission of urine, frequently. Some drops of urine

70


come off when coughing. Want of desire to urinate;
even when the bladder was full, she felt no desire to
urinate, but she was able to do so, whenever she pleased.
The urine has a strong ammoniacal odor, becomes turbid
and deposits a white-yellowish sediment, (a. 6 d ) Acrid,
offensively smelling urine, like violet root. A good deal
of walery, colourless urine, when the pain is felt. Pale,
clear urine. White, strongly smelling urine. Brown
urine, with sediment of red sand. Red urine, smelling of
sulphur, depositing a quantity of thick yellow mucus.
The urine when being emitted, is gold-yellow, and deposits
a whitish sediment, (a. 30 h.) Urine with a sediment of
white jiocculi. The urine deposits a brick-dust sediment.
Greasy pellicle on the urine with various colours. Yellow
sediment. The pale urine deposits a white crust on the
walls of the vessel. After micturition, in the morning,
tired unto lying down. Stitches in the urethra and anus.
After micturition, sluching pain in the fore part of the
urethra. Stitch from the neck of the bladder along the
penis. Cutting micturition, with expulsion of blood.
Burning in the urethra, with desire to urinate, in the
evening. Smarting pain in the glans, at the end of mic-
turition and afterwards, (a. 32 h.) When urinating after an
evacuation by the rectum, some drops of mucus come out
of the urethra, with pain in the perinaeum. Burning in
the urethra. Quick drawing to and fro, in the urethra, as
far as the bladder, with contractive sensation, (a. 10 d.)
Tension over the bladder.

Genital Organs.— Stitch in the glans, in the region
of the frenulum. Ulcer on the prepuce, healing rapidly.
Pain in the scrotum for several days. Violent drawing
in the testicles. Drawing-stretching pain in the spermatic
cords. Swelling of the spermatic cord, painful together
with the testicle, (the stool being loose.) Unusual irrita-
tion of the genital organs. Violent sexual desire. Sup-
pression of the sexuafdesire for a few days. Irresistible
desire for an embrace. Erection, without any sexual fan-
cies, in the evening. Powerful erections in an old man
fur the first seven days, then none at all for twenty-two
days, and again very violent from the 29th to the 43d day.
Erections day and night. Aversion to an embrace in a


71

man, (a. 25 d.) Emissions, soon after an embrace. Ner-
vous weakness in the loins, soon after an embrace. Dis-
charge of prostatic juice, during hard stools. Emissions,
without dream. Complete impotence. Aversion to an em-
brace,TM a female, (secondary effect ?) (a.25d.) Menses too
late, (a. 1 7, 22, 4 1 d.) Delay of the menses is a secondary
effect of Phosphorus. Menses too early and scanty. Ap-
pearance of the menses which had been suppressed for
many months. Discharge of blood from the uterus be-
tween the menstrual periods, (a. 9 d.) After a suspension
of eighteen months, (in a female of fifty-one years,) the
menses appear again for five days with violence, having a
bad smell. Bleeding of the ulcer previous to the appear-
ance of the menses. Violent toothache during the men-
strual flow, commencing at dinner. Colic during the menses.
Chilliness during the menses, with cold hands and feet.
Prickling itching of the varices during the menses. Sting-
ing itching of the whole body during the menses. Obtusion
of the head during the menses, and she feels so relaxed
that she falls asleep while reading. Violent pain in the
back, as if bruised, during the menses. During the menses
she feels very sick, especially in the evening, has pain in
the back as if bruised or torn, drawing in the whole body,
palpitation of the heart with anxiety, pinching across the
stomach with contractive pain, felt tired and faint unto fall-
ing, and felt so nauseated that she had to lie down. Sling-
ing pain in the forehead during the menses ; her eyes close.
Fever two days in succession during the menses ; the first
afternoon the fever begins with chilliness, followed by heat
and headache, without thirst ; on the second day, at noon,
chilliness for one hour, followed by spasmodic shaking of
the whole body, with chattering of 1eeth, then heal, espe-
cially in the head, and headache, (a. 10 d.) Swelling of
the gums and one cheek before and after the menses. At
the appearance of the menses violent nausea when sitting
up in the bed, sour vomiting, oppression of the chest, cold,
sweat on the forehead, and vertigo when walking. During
the menses cramp-like contraction of the lower limbs. A
few blotches, slinging and burning, on the margin of the
labia, for a fortnight. Stitches through the female pelvis.
Dull, tearing pain in the pudendum, as if ulcerated, during

72


and after a walk in the open air. Milk-like leucorrhcea.
Acrid, excoriating leucorrhcea, (a. 5 d.) Reddish leucor-
rhcea, (in an old person.) Tenacious leucorrhcea instead of
the menstrual discharge, (a. 20 d.) Profuse leucorrhcea
for seven days, (a. 9 d.)

Cold, Catarrh. — Frequent sneezing. Spasmodic
sneezing, with violent sensation in the head, contorsion of
the limbs, and constriction of the chest. Obstruction of
the nose, every morning. Feeling of dryness in the nose,
with sensation as if the walls would adhere to each other.
Discharge of mucus from the nose, without coryza. Dis-
charge of water from the nose in the open air, no mucus.
Green-yellow discharge from the nose. Clots in the nose.
Feeling of obstruction in the nose, with obtusion of the
head, as if a cold were approaching. Dry coryza. She
blows her nose all the time. Coryza, with heat in the

sections.label: head
sections.text:
Fluent coryza. Fluent coryza of one nostril, the
other being obstructed. Violent fluent coryza, with great
obtusion of the head, want of appetite and general sick
feeling, (a. 48 h.) Coryza, with inflammation of the throat
and great obtusion of the head.

Larynx and Trachea. — Tickling of the larynx two
nights in succession, inducing cough. Roughness of the
larynx and trachea. Roughness of the chest. Feeling of
dryness in the chest. Hoarseness in the morning. 1 he
larynx seemed furred, he is unable to utter a loud word.
Violent, catarrh with hoarseness. Catarrhal mucus in the
chest, in the morning. Cough, with stitching pain in the
hypochondria. Cough, with stitching pain under the pit of
the stomach ; she has to hold her chest. Sharp pressure
in the pit of the stomach, at every fit of cough. Sourish
vomiting during the cough. Pain in the stomach when
couohing. Pinching in the throat, exciting cough. Cough
from cold air, affecting his chest. Cough when eating,
loose, rattling, as in old people. Cough, with soreness of
the throat, after dinner. Cough in the open air, causing
pain in the chest and abdomen. Cough, especially when
drinking. Violent, dry cough when reading, in the evening.
Violent, dry cough when sitting- or lying down, not at all
during motion. Dry and hacking cough Violent dry
cou ah with oppressive headache. Dry troublesome cough


73

wakes her from sleep, fourteen nights in succession. Dry
cough with headache, as if the head would burst, with co-
ryza, (a. 35 d.) Hollow, mostly dry cough, with pressure
in the pit of the stomach, hindering sleep the whole night.
Titillation and cough, (a. 8 d.) Cough, with chilliness
over the whole body- Hollow cough, mostly in the morn-
ing and also at night. Loose cough, without expectora-
tion, with pain and sore feeling in the chest. Panting
cough, with sensation as if the chest was slightly furred,
and some expectoration, (a. 8 d.) Fatiguing cough, with
expectoration of tenacious mucus. Cough with white, tena-
cious expectoration. Cough in the morning, with translu-
cent expectoration, and sensation in the middle of the ster-
num, as if something had been torn loose.

sections.label: Chest
sections.text:
Continual cough with discharge of mucus and
tensive pain in the chest. Cough, day and night, with
expectoration of much mucus ; in a few days violent
stitches supervened in the chest. Muco-sanguineous ex-
pectoration when coughing, (a. 24 h.) Expulsion of floc-
culi of pus, with erosive burning behind the sternum.
Sensation in the throat, when coughing, as if a piece of
flesh were coming off. Short breathing after coughing.
Arrest of breathing during a quick walk, (a. some hours.)
Difficulty of breathing, in the evening when in bed, (a. 3
d.) Panting breathing when ascending a hill. Loud
rattling breathing. Anguish in the chest, in the evening.
Anxiety in the chest, with throbbing in the right side of
the chest. Frequent oppression of the chest, with nausea.
Oppression of the chest, worse when sitting, relieved by
eructations, (a. 22 d.) Sensation as if the chest were
oppressed by a load. Tightness of the chest as if bound
by a band. Tension and tightness in the chest. Tight-
ness in the chest, without asthma. Oppressive, tight
feeling in the chest. Sensation across the chest as if the
clothes were too tight. Oppression of the chest in the
morning, with palpitation of the heart and nausea, for one
hour. Contraction of the lungs. Contraction of the
chest, with pressure or clawing in the epigastrium.
Con! ractive pressing in the upper part of the left chest-
Oppressed breathing, with chilliness and violent headache,
he is scarcely able to collect his senses, (a. 1 h.) Op-

74


pression of the chest, as from congestion of blood, espe-
cially in the morning when waking. Cramp in the chest
after taking a drive, in the evening. Constrictive sensa-
tion in the upper part of the chest. Oppression of the
chest, as if the blood were pressing up in the throat quite
hot; in the morning, (a. 13 h.) Rush of blood to the

sections.label: chest
sections.text:
Rush of blood to the chest, at every emotion of
the mind, with cramp-like contraction between the sca-
pulae. Rush of blood to the heart, and palpitation of the
heart, very violent after dinner, (a. 9 d.) Palpitation of
the heart with anxiety, morning and evening. Palpitation
of the heart, frequently only 2 or 3 beats. A few strong
beats of the heart, when moving the left arm, when sitting
up in the bed, stretching the limbs, etc., going off again
when at rest. Stitches and stitching in various parts of
the chest, when sitting, sometimes with burning. Cutting
in the middle of the sternum, as far as the right scapula,
worse during an inspiration, less during motion, (4. d.)
Stitches in the left side of the chest when taking an
inspiration. Severe stitches in both sides of the chest,
both during motion and when at rest. Stitches in the
left side, under the ribs, for five days. Stitching in the
right side of the chest when breathing. Shootings in the
upper part of the chest. Stitches in the outer parts of the
chest, independent of breathing. Burning rising, from the
stomach into the chest, with anxiety, and with sweat cm
forehead and chest, when silting, (a. 2 h.) Pain in the
chest, especially during an inspiration. Pressure on the
lower part of the chest. Pressure on the upper part of
the chest from above downwards, followed by empty
eructations. Pain, as if bruised, in the upper part of the
chest, when stooping, moving or feeling the part. Itching
in the chest. Itching in the chest (trachea) and in the
pit of the throat, with dry cough which does not alleviate
the itching. Weakness of the chest. Violent soreness
of the pectoralis major. Soreness of the clavicle, per se
and when touched. Pain in the fleshy part of the right
chest, as if the glands where violently pressed upon.
Stitches in the mamma. Pain in the right side of the
chest, as if the skin were being raised with a pin. Tap-
pin* as with a finger on the right side of the chest, when


75

sitting. Warmth on the chest. Erysipelas of one of
the two mamma? covered with an eruption, with swelling,
redness, burning, stitching and final suppuration. Inflam-
mation and swelling of the left nipple and the whole of the
left mamma, with great tpain and suppurating after the
lapse of 10 days.

sections.label: Back
sections.text:
Pain of the os coccygis, as if ulcerated. Pain
in the os coccygis, hindering motion ; afterwards painful
stiffness in the nape of the neck, (2. d.) Pain in the
small of the back when raising the body after stooping,
and when standing, less when walking. Pain in the
small of the back after long sitting, a. (11 d.) Pain over
the os sacrum and the adjacent parts of the "Ossa ilia,
especially when stooping while sitting and after dinner,
with great faintness. Paralytic weakness of the small of
the back. Weakness of the small of the back, as if gone
to sleep, when sitting and when rising from a seat. Burn-
ing in the small of the back, especially when the menses
were delaying. Violent pain in the back, when silting
too long. Heaviness and weariness of the back, when
lying down. Periodically returning, intolerable pains in
the back, hindering walking. Unceasing stitching in the
spinal column, the whole day, at different hours, (a. 22 d.)
Violent stitch in the muscles of the back, above the left
hip., (a. 7 d.) Stitches into the lumbar vertebra?, extorting
screams. Pressure close below the scapulas. Pain in
the left scapula as of a plug being lodged there. Sensation
as if some one seized her on both scapulae, when lifting
and carrying something with both hands. Tearing in the
scapula?. Stitches in and under the scapula?. Stitching
pain in the right scapula. Jerking pain in the left sca-
pula. Beating and tearing in the right scapula.

sections.label: Neck
sections.text: Sensation as of a heavy load in the nape of the

sections.label: neck
sections.text:
Pressure in the nape of the neck. Stiffness of the
nape of the neck. Occiput and nape of the neck are* pain-
ful and quite stiff. Stiff neck. The anterior cervical
muscles are painful to the touch, or when moved. Stitches
in a tumor on the neck. Hard lump on the neck under
the chin, of the size of a hazel-nut, painful when touched.
Jerkings in the cervical muscles. Stitching pinchino- jn
the outer parts of the neck when walking in the open&air.

76 PHOSPHORUS.

Stitching in the front part of the neck towards the right
ear, and thence tearing extending into the vertex.

Upper Extremities.— Violently itching pimples in the
axilla, burning when scratched. Swelling of the axillary
glands, with burning pain in the skin of the arms. Violent
itching in the right axilla, and a glandular lump of the
size of a pea. Pressure and drawing in the shoulders.
The shoulder is painful when touched or moved. 1 he
shoulder-joints are painful when walking in the open air.
Tearing in the left shoulder, especially in the night.
Stitches in the right shoulder. Dull painful stitch in the
left shoulder. Boring in the right shoulder. Rheumatic
pain in the right shoulder, extending to the first ribs, for
one hour, (a. 7 d.) Rheumatic pain in the right shoulder,
in the morning when waking, (a. 36 h.) Pain as if
sprained in the right shoulder, especially when raising the
arm. Stitches in the axillae, through the shoulders. Dull
stitches in both axillae, broad and spreading out. Cracking
in the shoulder-joint. Heaviness in the shoulders and
arms, (a. 2 d.) Drawing stretching m the muscles of the
arm. from the shoulders down to the lower arm. Draw-
ing 'pain in the whole arm, increasing in the evening.
Tearing in the left arm and hand. The left arm goes to
sleep, with numbness of the fingers (without coldness) and
contraction of the same, especially in the morning ; after
which the arm becomes quite faint. The arm upon which
his head leans, goes to sleep. Itching of the arms.
Weakness of the arms, she was unable to move them m
the least, (a. 1 6 d.) Weakness of the joints of the arms,
with distension of the veins of the hands. Paralytic sore
pain in the arm, with tremor of the hand when holding
something. Pain of the right arm, as if sprained. Pain,
numbness and weakness of the right arm, - especially
around the elbow-joint, in the evening when lying
froing. off by changing the position of the part, but
returning soon after, and so on in frequent repetition.
Tearing in the outer surface of the right upper arm ; fric-
tion males it move to the lower arm where ^sultus of
the muscles becomes likewise' visible. Pain in right
upper arm as if bruised. Pain in the left humerus as if
bK drawmg, upwards and downwards, when sitting,


77

Rheumatic pain in the right upper arm, after a slight
cold. Tearing in the upper arm. Great weariness of
the upper arm. Burning of the skin of both upper arms.
Painful pressure in the periosteum of the humerus and
the trochlea, resembling bone-pain, (a. 6 h.) Pain of the
elbow-joint as if broken. Tearing and drawing in the
right elbow-joint. Tearing in the inner side of the fore-
arm, as if the bone were being torn out, going off by fric-
tion. Tearing and boring from the elbow to the shoulder.
Tearing and stitching in \he right elbow. Stitches in the
elbow-joint after a fright, afterwards in an excoriated place
of the foot. Gnawing pain in the elbow, extending to-
wards the shoulder. Shock and jerking in the olecranon
processes of both arms. Red tips, with corrosive itching
on a space of the size of the hand, in the bend of the right
elbow. Violent tearing of the inner side of the left fore-
arm, as if the skin were being torn off. Tearing in the
fore-arms, especially around the wrist-joints. Tearing in
the wrist-joint, with paralytic weakness, in the evening.
Pain as if sprained in the wrist-joint. Tearing in the
metacarpal bones. Tearing in the hand, especially the
knuckles, generally in the night when in bed. Darting in
the knuckles and thumb. Drawing in the hands and
fingers, after moistening them with tepid water. Creep-
ing of the hands in the open air, when yawning, (a. i h.)
Heaviness and tremor of the hands, when letting the arms
hang, with redness and distended veins, with sensation as
if much blood were pressing into the veins. Determina-
tion of blood to the hands and head, as if coming from
the stomach, the veins on the dorsa of the hands being
distended. Cold hands. Tremor of the hands. One
hand occasionally feels paralysed, for several hours. Both
hands had gone to sleep, in the morning when waking,
(21. d.) Itching of the hands. The skin on the hands
was rough and dry. Warts form on the hands. Vesicles
as from the heat, on the dorsa of both hands, with itching,
worst in the night. Burning feeling in the hands, without
any external heat. Burning feeling in the palms of the
hands. Intensely painful stitches in the wrist-joint, when
at rest, (a. 17 d.) Sudden swelling of the hand and fin-
gers. Swelling of the wrist-joint, with throbbing in the

78


same as if in an ulcer, and tearing extending into the
fingers, even when at rest and still much worse when
moving the stiff wrist-joint, (after a cold ?) ' Pain in the
thumb, as if sprained, when seizing something. Swelling
ol the posterior joint of the thumb, painful when touching
it and experiencing a tensive pain during motion. Pain
as if sprained, or as if strained, in the posterior joint of
the thumb, during motion. Pain, as if sprained, in the
finger joints, (a. 6 d.) The fingers of one hand feel numb
and insensible, those of the other feeling as if they had
gone to sleep. The middle-finger of the right hand be-
comes quite numb, dead, bloodless and cold, in moderately
cold air. Jerking of single fingers. Paralytic jerkings
sometimes, in the right thumb when writing, he is unable
to hold his pen. Periodical contraction of the fingers,
like cramp. Weakness and jerking in one finger, the
whole day. Violent jerking in the left little finger.
Heaviness in the tips of the fingers. Cramp-hke drawing
and tearing in the little finger. Tearing in the right little
finger. Paralysis of the fingers ; they are able to feel, but
scarcely able to be moved. Tension in the fingers of the
left hand. Tension in the fourth and fifth fingers of both
hands, as if sprained. Painful swelling of a finger,
especially painful when knocking it against something.
Chronic panaritium, which refuses to heal. Cracked skin
of the finger-joints, as if by cold.

Lower Extremities. — Pain of the nates as of sub-
cutaneous ulceration, when sitting too long. Pulsation in
the.nates. Twitchings in the nates. Visible, but painful
twitching in one of the nates and in the thigh. Pain of
the left hip-joint. Painful paralytic feeling in the left hip,
in the evening, making it almost impossible for him to
tread on that foot ; no pain when sitting or lying down.
Sensation in the region of the right hip as if held fast, no
pain when sitting. Violent pain in the fold of the left hip.
Pain in the hips as if sprained. Stitching in the left hip,
going off by friction. Violent stitch in the right hip, to-
wards the chest. Itching -of the hips. Great weakness
in the lower limbs; she falls easily- The left limb goes
to sleep, without any apparent cause. Severe paralytic
sensation in the right limb, at night. Weariness in the


79

limbs early. The limbs are painful in the morning, as
after a Ions* journey on foot. Tension in the left limb and
painful stiffness with pressure. Cramp-like contractive
sensation in both limbs and feet, with jerks. Violent ach-
ing in the left ischium, when sitting too long. Great rest-
lessness in the limbs, with icy-cold hands, especially in the
evening. Violent drawing to and fro in the thigh, during
the siesta. Drawing pain in the thighs, relieved by walk-
ing. Momentary, tearing pain in the left thigh, commenc-
ing at the knee. Tearing jerks in the posterior side of the
thigh, extending to the knee, during and after a walk in the
open air, every four minutes, with soreness of the spot
when touching it. Burning of the thigh, increased by
contact. Pain as from bruises in the middle of the thigh ;
the spot is painful to the touch, the pain hindering walk-
ing. Itching of the thigh and the region of the patella.
Severe itching of a small spot of the thigh, with smarting
after scratching. Large pimples on the posterior sides of
the thighs, painful to the touch. Soreness of the inner
sides of the thighs. Herpes over the knees and below the
patella. Continual coldness in the knees, at night when
in bed. Trembling of the knees. Cramp-like drawing
in the knee when walking. Tearing in the knees in the
open air, several evenings. Violent tearing along the in-
ner side of the calf, as if the flesh were being torn loose,
going off by friction ; after dinner. Drawing pain from
the knees to the feet. Drawing from the knee to the foot,
every drawing being followed by a painful jerk, (a. 15 d.)
Tearing in the bend of the right knee, at night. Stretching
of the hamstrings when walking, as if too short. Arthritic
stretching in the knees, as if sprained ; they feel hot to the
hands. Paralytic feeling in the left knee. Pain as if
sprained in the left knee. Dull pain around the left knee-
joint. Nightly stitching in the knees, in paroxysms. Stitch
in the inner surface of the right knee, at every step ; pain
as if bruised over the knee, when sitting or when raising
the thigh ; the pain disappears when rising. Tearing from
the knee to the dorsum of the foot, the forepart of the left
foot having gone to sleep, going off by friction. Suddenly
forming, red, inflamed, smarting and painful excrescence
between the calf and bend of the knee. Tension in

80


the right calf when walking. Cramp in the calf. Cramp
in the calf, and the leg is jerked upwards when stretching
it while walking. The leg from the calf to the foot has
gone to sleep, as if the circulation had been stopped by
tying the leg up below the knee. Violent itching of the
calves and tibiae. Pain of the tibiae when walking. Pain
in the tibiae as if bruised. Pain, as if bruised, in the peri-
osteum of the tibiae, painful when touched. Tearing
stitches in the tibiae. A number of small spots like freckles
on the lower part of the tibiae. A number of small, brown-
red spots on the legs, like petechia?. Pain in the left tar-
sal joint, extending upwards to the calf. Violent tearing
and stitching in ttie feet, hindering sleep in ihe night.
Tearing in the inner border of the left sole. Tearing in
the left ankle, 'in the night. Violent itching of the soles
and toes, in the evening. Formication in the feet and toes.
Creeping under the toes. Tingling in the feet, at night.
Pain in the tarsal joint when walking, as if sprained,
stretching when treading, (a. 4 d.) The tarsal joint is
easily sprained or bent when treading. Paralytic
feeling in the feet. Icy-cold feet, even when in bed, (in
June.) Paralytic drawing pain in the ankles, extending
into the knee. Sweaty feet. Heaviness of the feet, asif
swollen. Swelling of the tendons of the right ankle.
Swelling of the feet, in the evening, (a. 7 d.) Spots on
the feet. Increase of vesicles and ulcers on the feet.
Stitches in the swelling of the foot. Stitching pain in the
right ankle, the parts being swollen, very painful when
treading. Pain of the soles, as if he had gone too far ;
they are red. Troublesome feeling of dryness in the soles,
(a. 27 d.) Cramp in the soles of the feet. Jerks in the
feet, with tingling cramp in the soles. Jerks and shootings
in the feet. Tearing stitchingSn both soles. Beating pain
in the heels, at night, she is obliged to rub them warm, to
alleviate the pain. The feet feel weak and as if gone to
sleep, with great restlessness. Creeping in both heels.
Tension in the heels, in the morning when in bed. Blis-
ter on the heel, bursting open, emitting a humour, and
very painful when walking, (a. 14 d.) The heels and toes
which had been frozen previously, become very painful,
especially in the shoes when walking, (a. 48 h.) Itching


81

under the toes and feet. Violent stitches in the ball of
the bi<r toe, with inflammation. Chilblains come on in
March? (a. 9 d.) Stitches in the big toe of the left foot,
mostly during motion and in the evening. Tearing in the
toes when silting, going off by friction. Pain of the big
toe as if frozen. Jerkings in the left big toe, when sitting.
Violent stitch in the right big toe. Pains in the corns
piercing bone and marrow. Violent, stitching pressure in
the corns, as if boring into them with a knife. Stitching
in the corns when walking. Old corns on the little toe be-
come painful, the toe swells.

General Symptoms. — Formication and itching in the
paralysed parts. General itching of the body, (22. d.)
Itching of the back and bends of the knees. Violent itch-
ing, ii°the night, of the arms, legs, back, and abdomen, (a.
12 d.) Itching and gnawing of the abdomen, arms and
thighs ; scratching brought on red streaks, (a. 26, 27 d.)
Itching of the whole body at night, with much heat and
dryness of the mouth, (a. 12 h.) Burning itching of the
whole body, (a. 10 d.) Frequent prickings in the skin.
Scattered stitches, with pressure, in various parts of the
body. Itching, large vesicles over the whole body, also
in the face. Round herpetic spots over the whole body.
Blotches and blotch-like spots, brownish and bluish-red.
Brownish, dark, sometimes elevated spots in the bends of
the knees, on the chest, forehead, and under the corner of
the mouth. Blotches in the skin of the nates. Painful
hard blisters in various spots, not itching. Blisters, burst-
ing open, with humor. Itching vesicles between the fin-
gers and in the bend of the knee. Small boils on the nape
of the neck, chest and thighs. Large boils on the thighs,
chest and forehead. Sore, excoriated spots upon the skin,
with redness, or smarting and stinging pain. Scaling off
of the epidermis. Itching of the wart on the forehead.
Burning in a wart as in a suppurating wound, in the even-
ing after lying down. Pinching contractive pain in a cica-
trix. Black blood is oozing from the cicatrix of an old
vesicatory. Tensive drawing in the glands, also on the

sections.label: neck
sections.text:
Increased feeling of warmth in the paralyzed parts.
Burning in the hands and legs. Burning on the arms and
thighs. Burning of the whole right side of the body.


Stitching in the chest and back, also in the right arm, dur-
ing motion, especially in the night when in bed, (a. 11 d.)
Drawing in arms and legs, with weeping mood, (a. 13 d.)
Tearing in the right fore-arm and knee, as soon as she be-
comes cold. Most of the symptoms cease in the after-
noon after dinner. Sensitiveness to cool weather. His
pain increases when a change of the weather is approach-
ing. Catches cold easily in the open air, bringing on colic,
pain in the nape of the neck, stiffness of the arms, tooth-
ache, lachryrnations, hiccough, cutting and stitching in and
above the pit of the stomach, obtusion of the head, or at <
last cold and damp-cold feet and hands, with hot cheek,
etc. Sort of coryza on a walk. Catarrhal feeling through
the whole body, with chilliness and drowsiness. A slight
wetting or cold of the feet brings on weariness in all the
limbs, burning of the hands, headache ; has to go to bed ;
next day coryza. Catarrh and toothache when rising, after
having slightly perspired during the night, with slight jerks
in the teeth. Agitation of the blood. In the night he thinks
he hears the blood rush through the body. Orgasm of the
blood, with chilliness and trembling, and anxiety in the in-
testines. Profuse bleeding of small wounds. Hemorrhage
from various parts of the body, haemoptysis, bleeding of the
gums, varices, etc. Profuse sweat from slight sweating.
Heat in the head and chest when talking animatedly. Sen-
sation as if all the limbs were stretched, when performing
quick motions. Hands and feet go to sleep. Deadness
of the hands and feet. Rigor of the hands and feet and

sections.label: nose
sections.text:
A sort of insensibility in the whole body. Cold-
ness, want of warmth in the whole body. Icy coldness
of the hands and feet the whole day, also when in bed.
Chilliness when sitting, not when walking. Hysteric
weakness, she is unable to move a limb, with constant gnaw-
ing, gulping-up and torture and pressure in the chest. Con-
slant yawning and watery urine during the paroxysm of pain.

Weakness, Fits.— Tremulous in the morning, with
perceptible twitching of the limbs; (a. 8 d.) Chattering of
teeth and general trembling, in the morning when waking.
Tremor" of the hands. Tremor of the thighs, like shud-
dering. Trembling of the chest and hands, as if she had
taken too much coffee. Sick feeling in the whole body,


83

especially the stomach. Emaciation, especially of the
hands. Hectic fever and emaciation. Convulsions Death
bv ffanerene and inflammation ; in one case the body shone
in all its parts. Pain in all the limbs. The pains are worst
from afternoon till morning. The limbs feel bruised. All
the joints are painful, especially during motion. J?aint
feeling as of being bruised, not. disposed to do anything.
Pale °and bruised all over. Bruised ieehng and heaviness
in the left knee and elbow. Hands and feet feel weak as
if not existing. Heaviness of the hands and feet. Heavi-
ness of the mind and body. Painful heaviness of ihe whole
body, now of the head, now the chest, now the thighs and
legs, now all over, making him indolent and' putting him
out of humor ; the heaviness is preceded by a general, ex-
hausting sweat. Hands and feet are heavy as lead.
Heaviness of the limbs, before rising. Faintness and
weakness in the joints, especially the knee-joints, during
motion and when sitting, (a. 14 d.) Feeling of looseness
in the knee-joint, he is scarcely able to stand. Weakness
and faintness in the limbs, especially the knee-joints, with
stinging and burning ; sometimes most after rising and ag-
gravated by rest, relieved by walking, for several days.
Great weakness in the limbs, for upwards of three weeks.
Great weakness in the morning when rising and during the
day, general sick feeling, heart-burn, and after a quick
walk canine hunger and trembling of the limbs. Walking
exhausts him very much. Frequent and sudden attacks
of great weakness. General, sudden, excessive weakness.
Sudden, general weakness, win heat in the face, (a. 11 d.)
Faint, oppressed feeling the whole day. Weariness of the
whole body, especially "of the thighs, in a robust man, (a.
9 d.) Relaxation for several days, especially in the chest.
Sensation in chest and abdomen, as if every thing would
break down. Paralytic feeling after sitting, for some min-
utes. Sick and paralytic feeling in the body. Loss of
strength in all the limbs, especially the joints, with good
appetite. The whole right side feels paralysed, with nau-
sea. He walks like one paralytic, without noticing it him-
self. As if paralysed mentally and bodily, in the morning
and the whole day- As if paralysed in the back and arms,
after the siesta. "Tired and drowsy, aftej drinking a glass

84


of wine in the afternoon, had to sleep a few hours, (a. 48
h.) Complete loss of all strength. Fainting fit.

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
Tries to gape all the time, but does not suc-
ceed. Frequent, yawning with chilliness. Drowsiness af-
ter dinner. Sleeplessness and restlessness, (a. 36 h.)
Light sleep. She was unable to fall asleep, owing to a
feeling as if the eyes did not close, but had to be kept
closed with the hands and turned about their axis in the
head, (a. 6 d.) After waking up in the evening and at
night he has great difficulty in falling asleep again. Is
unable to fall asleep. Can only rest on the right side.
Lying upon the left side gives him an anxiety, (a. 19 d.)
A general sick feeling prevents sleep until 2 o'clock.
Restless sleep, with lascivious dreams and emissions, after
which he slept but little. Wakes up in the evening with
violent vertigo and nausea. Dull pain in the haunch-bones
in the evening when in bed, as if he had been lying upon
too hard a couch ; he had to alter his position all the time ;
went off in the morning. After the siesta the back felt
sprained or as if gone to sleep-. Wakes up in the night
from pressure as if upon the bladder. Violent drawing in
the right upper and lower limb, in the [night. Sensation
as if having spoiled one's stomach in the night. Intoler-
able itching of the hands, in the evening when in bed.
Intense prickling itching of both dorsa of the hands,
preventing him from sleeping ^ scratching does no good.
Nightly eructations as of putrid eggs. Great thirst in the
night. Restless night, from pressure at the stomach and
nausea. Pain in the lower limbs as if bruised, in the
night, or as if from excessive weariness. The external
ear is painful during the night. Violent stitches through
the ear and teeth in the night. Frequent boring in the
tooth, in the night. Violent palpitations of the heart at
nio-ht, (5 nights.) He wakes up with colic at 1 o'clock
in°the night, (a. 21 d.) He wakes every night after mid-
night in a state of discouragement. When sleeping, even
in°day-time, the saliva flows out of his mouth. Pressure
in the abdomen, in the night. Nightly spasm of the
chest ; he is near suffocating. He wakes up in the night
with sensation as if the larynx and trachea had become
much narrower, he feels suffocating. Inclination to vomit


85

at night, and continual eructation tasting of the ingesta.
He is roused from sleep in the night by obstruction of the
nose and difficulty of breathing. A kind of vertigo, in
the evening when in bed and turning to the other side, as
if all the blood were rushing to the head. Vertigo in the
evening when in bed, as if the bed were turning in a cir-

i cle. In the night when waking up, he feels stupefied, in-
toxicated, giddy. Drowsy, a sort of giddiness, without
being able to sleep. Sopor in day-time. Starting when
about to fall asleep. As soon as he falls asleep, he has
anxious dreams and then wakes again. She is so uneasy
in the evening that she cannot fall asleep ; she feels the
same uneasiness when waking up, (a. 5 d.) Great anx-
iety and restlessness as soon as she goes to bed in the
evening. Anxiety the whole night, no heat, as if he had
committed murder, with constant tossing about. Illusion
when falling asleep, as if somebody were seizing him by

i the throat, with the intention of throttling him, (a. 4 d.)

I She wakes towards morning with a start. She wakes
with anxiety every morning. Frequent waking in the
night with chilliness. Starting when asleep. Torment-
ing dreams about vermine. Tossing about and moaning
the whole night, with anxious dreams. Anguish during a
state of sopor with absence of consciousness, still weep-

i ing, writhing of the hands, as if in despair, lamentations,
tossing about, short breathing ; she seizes those around
her shyly or lays hold of them with vehemence. Heat and
dryness of the mouth in the night, she has to drink a
good deal, for some nights. Frequent waking in the
night, from feeling too hot, without sweat. Dry heat in
the night without thirst, with pain of the parts upon which
she had lain. Waking from anxious dreams in the night,
after which chilliness and tremor of the whole body, espe-
cially in the abdomen, violent orgasm of the blood and
oppression of the chest, hindering breathing and scarcely
permitting him to breathe, (a. 10 d.) Uneasy a long lime
previous to falling asleep ; after which she wakes with
oppression of the chest as of a load, aggravating the
breathing, (a. 22 d.) Confused dreams. Vexed dreams.
Sleep full of dreams. He sleeps on his back, with his
left hand under the occiput. Restless at night and dream-

86


ing constantly. Heavy anxious dreams towards morning.
Vivid dreams, about affairs with which he could not get
along. Anxious dreams, (a. 48 h.) Dreams full of care
about something which she had to attend to, and for the
sake of which she gets up continually. Exclamations
and conversations in her sleep. Anxious dreams about
biling animals, she cries out and wakes. Dreams she
is stung by an insect behind the ears. Dreams that some
one pinches her back, chest, etc, and that he tickles her
soles. Dream about robbers. Dream about fire, with
screams and kicking about. Dream about a hemor-
rhage. Sad dreams. Frightful dreams. Funny dreams.
Historical dreams every night. Dreams about dead per-
sons and quarrels. Drowsiness by day, and even before
dinner. Feels as if he had not slept enough in the morn-
ing. Sleep does not refresh her. As if paralysed and
bruised in the morning after rising, (a. 6 d )

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Cool feeling in the whole body. Concealed
chilly tremulousness in the whole body, even near a warm
stove. Chilly hands, although they feel warm to others
and their veins are distended. Chilliness in the evening,
and falling asleep from weakness ; towards midnight
wakes up from heavy dreams, with profuse sweat all
over. Cold limbs. Shuddering, cannot be reheved by
the warmth of the stove. Shuddering over the whole
body, without chilliness. Chill over the back. Chill
over the back from below upwards, in day-time, kre-
quenl chilliness, the first days. Chilliness, several even-
ings, after going to bed. Chilliness, every evening, with
shuddering, without thirst, but with dryness in the throat.
Chilliness and shuddering, no appetite, no subsequent
heat Chilliness every afiernoon, and famtness ior seve-
ral days. ('hills with shaking, next night sweat, great
uneasiness the day before, for two days, (9 d.) Violent
chill ; cold thrill over the back, he had to he down and
cover himself, becoming warm very gradually ; when put-
tin * a hand from under the cover, he felt a new chill ;
the°hands felt rigid with cold, the head feehng a dull pa.n j
no subsequent heat, (a. 26 h.) Internal chilliness, several

PHOSPHORIC ACID.

^Add sulphuric acid to a pound of calcined bones broken
in pieces, and stir up the mixture several times in twenty-
four hours with a glass tube. Add to this amalgam two
pounds of brandy or rum, mix it, tie up the whole in a
linen bag, and press it between two smooth boards,
usincr heavy weight for that purpose. The residue con-
tained in the bag, may again be mixed with two more
pounds of brand v to be pressed out again as before. ± ne
liquid obtained by the second pressing, may then be mixed
with the former and may be left standing a couple ot days
under cover, for the purpose of allowing the liquid time to
settle. The clear liquid which is poured off, is inspissated
over the fire in a porcelain cup previously warmed, and is
melted by a red heat. The melted phosphoric acid ought
to be clear as crystal. When yet warm, it is broken in
pieces and kept in a well-corked vial, inasmuch as it be-
comes converted into a clear, thickish liquid when expos-
ed to the air. . . ,

Camphor moderates the effect of phosphoric acid.

Singing when sleeping. He frequently bites his tongue in

Dreams causing anxiety. Dreams before and after mid-

quent starting at night, as if he were falling from a height

noon, with blue nails, tearing in the wrist-joints and para-
lytic weakness of the arms. Chilliness with trembling,
in the evening ; next morning heat in the face, dryness in

Violent chills from afternoon till evening, followed by dry
heat, so violent that he almost lost his senses on account of

limbs, every evening, rousing her from sleep ; no subse-
quent heat. Chilliness and coldness for hours, towards
evening, without any subsequent thirst or heat. Alterna-
tion of shiverings and heat, in the evening. Frequent al-
ternation of chilliness and heat, in the evening ; dry heat
in the face without redness, with chilliness ; after the ter-
mination of the heat, the chilliness returns with more vio-
lence, it is a cold thrill over the whole body ; profuse sweat
towards morning when he had fallen asleep again after
waking. Feeling of chilliness in the face, temples, on the
forehead, as if a cold breeze blew upon the parts, with feel-

cheek, the left feeling warm, the external temperature be-

“Mental enfceblement” is the thought that will come into the mind
when considering what the Phosphoric acid patient says, does and
looks. The mind seems tired. When questioned he answers slowly or
does not speak, but only looks at the questioner. He is too tired to talk
or even think. He says : “Don’t talk to me ; let me alone.” This state
is found in both acute and chronic diseases. He is so tired in mind,
perfectly exhausted. In chronic diseases when brought on from long
study ; prolonged worry in business men ; in feeble school girls, who
become relaxed from very little effort. In acute diseases he, especially
in typhoid fever, is averse to speaking or answering questions. He
merely looks. Finally he rouses up and says: “Don’t talk to me, I am
so tired.” He cannot think what he wishes to say, cannot frame his
answers to questions. Another cause is sexual excesses in young men,
or in those guilty of secret vice. Weakness ; lack of reaction ; state of
stupor, with impotency ; mental prostration, and as if the spine had
given out.

In every case we find the mental symptoms are the first to develop.
The remedy runs from the mental to the physical, from the brain to the
muscles. This is so striking that it is contrasted with Muriatic acid.
In the latter remedy the muscular prostration comes first, and the mind
seems clear until long after the muscles arc prostrated. In Phosphoric
acid the muscles seem strong after the mind has given out. The pa-
tient seems vigorous physically. He says he is all right physically, can
work, can exercise even violently ; but the mind is tired, there is mental
apathy, he can not add up a column of figures, can not read the news-
paper and carry the trend of thought, can not connect circumstances.
He forgets the names of those in his family ; a business man forgets
the names of his clerks ; he is in confusion. Yet he can exercise, can
go out and walk ; the weakness in the muscles will come later.

Phosphoric acid has also great physical weakness ; so tired in the
back so tired in the muscles ; so tired all over ; a paralytic weakness.
Later there is sexual impotence ; aversion to coition ; loss of sexual de-

In Phosphoric acid there is often an amelioralion of complaints by
their ending in a diarrhoea. Copious, thin, watery stool. From the
quantity it would seem that the patient would be exhausted. Child
with copious, watery, stool in summer ; so copious that the napkin
seems of no use ; the stool runs all over the mother’s dress and on the
floor forming great puddles ; the stool is almost odorless, thin and
watery, and the little one smiles as if nothing were the matter. The
mother wonders where it all comes from, and yet the child seems well.
The Phosphoric acid diarrhoea often ameliorates many of the symp-
toms and the patient feels better. Chronic diarrhoea, copious, thin and
watery, whitish gray, and the patient feels comfortable, free and
happy. If the diarrhoea slacks up the patient is worse and on come
symptoms of tuberculosis, weakness, prostration, brain-fag. Some
patients say they arc never comfortable unless they have diarrhoea.
Podophyllum is the very opposite. Take the same child ; the stool is
very copious and runs all over the floor, the mother wonders where it
all comes from, but the stool is offensive, a horrible stench, and
the patient looks as if dying ; mouth and nose drawn, countenance hip-
pocratic ; almost unconscious. There is painless stool in both, but
Phosphoric acid has not the great prostration. In Phosphoric acid the
stool is whitish gray, like dirty white paint ; in Podophyllum it is
yellow. Gratiola has a similar state of prostration, but the fluid is

The tendency of the Phosphoric acid patient at the end of the brain

and exhaustion. During^ the prostration tuberculosis frequently develops ;

stage of an inflammatory swelling of the gum and soft parts of the mouth,
extending over the face and neck, associated with the development of
masses of osteophyte of varying extent and thickness about the jaw ; in
the second stage the teeth become black, the gum recedes, the osteophytes
suppurate, and the jaw becomes denuded, rough, and blackish or grayish-
green, and the teeth fall out; this stage is associated with the most violent
pain in the face and head, disturbance of digestion, sleeplessness, fever,
salivation, fistulous burrowing of the matter in the muscles and integu¬
ments of the face, which became erysipelatous, followed by exfoliation of
the bone, and sometimes by extension of the necrosis to all the bones of
the skull, and death with hectic fever,*’. — Necrosis of the jaw ; the disease
begins as toothache, involving one or more teeth in the upper or lower
jaw; the disease spreads to the jawbone, which increases in volume and
becomes painful to pressure ; afterwards the soft parts become swollen,
especially the gums and cheeks, in the latter erysipelatous inflammation
develops, even extending over the whole side of the face and dowm on to
the neck ; the patients have fever, yellow color of the skin, especially of
the face, loss of appetite, thirst, irregular stools ; the pain at last extends
to the ear and temple, with increased secretion of saliva. Various teeth
become loose, and between them there is a discharge of offensive matter,
that collects in various parts of the jaw under the gum or under the skin
externally, and gradually makes its way into the mouth or through the
skin, usually by a number of circuitous channels. The teeth fall out, the
jaw becomes denuded, and the necrosis either becomes circumscribed or in¬
volves the whole jaw,”. — Diseases of the gums and maxillary bones, termi¬

was also no muscular atrophy. The optic nerve was extremely irritable,
reflex optic symptoms could be produced not only by irritation of the tri¬
geminus, but also from the nape of the neck, from the lower angle of the
scapula, and often from the upper arm. The auditory nerve was normal,
though exhibiting some symptoms of hypersesthesia. The patient was
gradually cured by electricity.

Phos, stands at the head of haemorrhagics, and corresponds
to the haemorrhagic diathesis. The blood loses its coagulability.
Very small wounds bleed profusely. Blood-streaked discharges are
very characteristic when from lungs, nose, bowels, or other orifices.
Haemorrhoids. Menses are more profuse and longer-lasting than usual.
There may be vicarious menstniation in the form of haemoptYsis,
epistaxis, or haematuria. Left ovarian pain. Leucorrhoea which
causes blisters. Sexual excitement is great in both sexes, going to
the extent of satyriasis and nymphomania. Frequent erections in
men, and sexual thoughts entirely beyond the patient's control.
Erections in spite of efforts to control passion in young men. Impo-
tence from over-indulgence or from celibacy. The female breasts are
the seat of many burning, shooting, cramping pains, and Phos. has
proved a leading remedy in mammary abscess and fistulae. The charac-
teristics are : Erysipelatous appearance } red streaks starting from
opening ; thin, ichorous discharge. The haemorrhagic action of Phos. is
seen in many forms of pulmonary haemorrhage and congestion : blood-
streaked or rusty sputa ; tasting salty ; when patients with delicate
chests bring up phlegm tinged with blood whenever they take cold
Phos. will generally clear up the case. Phthisis florida may also need
Phos. It has also a " stomach- " or " liver- '* cough ; cough comes on
after eating, and starts from a tickling in pit of stomach. Cough <
when strangers enter the room. Cough < from strong odours (part
of the general sensitiveness of the drug). Bronchial catarrh > in all
grades may require it. Cough ss tearing pain under sternum as if
something was being torn loose. Su£Eocative pains in upper part of
chest with constriction of larynx and engorgement of lungs ; mucous
rales ; panting and laboured breathing, even emphysema. After the
cough an asthmatic attack. The Conditions of Pnos. will generally
decide when it should be given. T. D. Stow (y. of Homceopathics,
August, 1890) reports the case of H. B., 52, farmer, who had for six
months a sharp pain with soreness in third intercostal space, three
inches to left of sternum, limiting inspirations. Dyspnoea on exercise ;
dry cough during the day till 10 p.m. Thick, yellow, sweetish sputa
from 6 a.m. to 10 a.m. Cough < lying on left side ; when talking ;
when eating and just after eating ; on going into cold air ; by change
of weather. > In fairly warm room ; lying on right side. Prefers
cold food. Has become alarmed by the persistence of the attack and
loss of flesh. Three doses of Phos. 500 (Dunham), taken on three

Whenever she washes clothes or walks fast she has — ^rush of blood to

) Allied to the rheumatic symptoms of Phos, is its sensitiveness
to effects of storms, especially thunderstorms. Phos, has cured more
cases of headache always coming on when thunderstorms are about
than any other remedy in my experience. It has also cured blindness
from lightning stroke. The headaches from inhaling the steam of a
washtub perhaps come in the same category as effects of vapour-
laden air when storms are about. Mills (quoted H. W,, xxxi. 33)
relates a typical case of thunderstorm effect : Mrs. F., tall, thin, dark,
of mild and gentle disposition, was seen by the doctor during a
thunderstorm. He found her sitting on the stairs, trembling and cold
and bathed in cold, clammy sweat, full of nervous dread, and almost
beside herself. One dose of Phos, cm cured. Some weeks later she
witnessed a worse storm with complete unconcern. The power of
Phos, over septic conditions is illustrated in a case of Howard
Crutcher's (quoted H, W,^ xxxiii. 405). A girl, 16, had perforating
appendicitis, operation having been delayed too long in consequence
of opposition of friends. Although he deemed it useless he was per-
suaded to operate, and found a large abscess behind the colon, freely
communicating with the peritoneal cavity. Up to the fourth day the
patient progressed favourably. Then there was a collapse : pulse
130, mind wandering, urine and faeces passed without restraint. The
patient was rapidly sinking ; Atsen. gave no help. The doctor sent
word to the students who were nursing the patient that they might
try a hot saline enema. On attempting to give it \h^rectum was found
to be open, no resistance being offered by the sphincter. Greyish-white
f cecal discharges, watery and offensive, passed constantly, " The students,
recognising the indication for Phos,, gave a dose of that remedy, and
instead of dying the girl got well.'' Peculiar sensations are : As if
about to die. As if immersed in hot water. Anxiety as if below left
breast. As if he had been lying at night with head too low. As if
everything had stopped in head. As if chair were rising. As if eyes
would be pressed out ; or pressed down by weight about them. As
if painful nodes under scalp. As if pulled by hair. As if head would
burst. As if something exploded in head. As if skin of face too
tight. As if something were pulled tight over ears. As if dust in
right eye ; sand in left eye ; eyeballs large. As if something lay
before ears ; foreign body in ears. As if nose stuck together. As if
nails driven into jaws. As if food did not digest properly. As if
